newsitem.title: GERMANY: Only 15 pct of Germans want EMU in 1999 - survey.
newsitem.headline: Only 15 pct of Germans want EMU in 1999 - survey.

text.p: Only 15 percent of Germans want Economic and Monetary Union to go ahead on schedule in 1999, while 41 percent oppose the project and 38 percent want a postponement, a survey showed on Friday.

The survey was carried out by the FORSA research institute for Deutsche Welle television. A representative sample of 1,000 Germans was asked on November 13 and 14 when monetary union should take place.
Germany's coalition government is struggling to bring its state finances in order to meet qualification terms next year to join the planned launch of the euro currency in 1999.
But Finance Minister Theo Waigel is determined to fulfil the Maastricht treaty criteria so as to keep the faith of Germans attached to their stable mark ahead of parliamentary elections in 1998.
